short: The monthly or quarterly return listing everything you sold.
seoTitle: GSTR-1 — Meaning and Example for Businesses
metaDescription: The monthly or quarterly return listing everything you sold. It is what feeds your customers' input tax credit. Part of the free Setu business glossary.
definition: GSTR-1 is the return in which a registered business reports its outward supplies — invoice-wise for B2B sales, summarised for B2C, plus credit notes, debit notes and an HSN summary. It is what feeds your customers' input tax credit.
bodyHtml:
Why GSTR-1 matters

What you file in GSTR-1 becomes visible to every one of your business customers. Miss an invoice and their credit disappears; report one twice and your own liability inflates.

How GSTR-1 works in practice

The clean version of this workflow is a billing system that already holds invoice numbers, GSTINs, taxable values, rates and HSN codes, so the return is an export rather than a retyping exercise.

faq.question: How often is GSTR-1 filed?
faq.answer: Monthly for larger taxpayers, quarterly for those opted into the quarterly filing scheme with monthly tax payment.

faq.question: Can I revise a filed GSTR-1?
faq.answer: There is no revision as such. Corrections are made through amendments in a later period's return.
